Neper looks progress

One widget set, five platform flavors in priority order (Windows, Linux, Neper, macOS / iOS, Android), each in a Light and a Dark look (docs/ui/looks-plan.md). Generated from docs/ui/looks/status.json and status.d by scripts/render_looks.py; updated 2026-10-19 23:23:00. 30 Delphi-equivalent controls and 17 platform idiom controls. A look with no status entry whose picture exists is shown as started: rendered from the platform palette, not compared with a real screen.

Completion is the weighted share of the 30 Delphi-equivalent controls in each look: planned 0 %, started 20 %, review 60 %, matched or ready 100 %. Overall is the mean of the five flavors; each flavor is the mean of its Light and Dark look. The weights are a rough measure of how close a control is, not an audit result; an independent audit sets the statuses (docs/ui/looks/audit.md). Matched means every state that has a real capture reproduces it; states with no capture stay unverified, so nothing reaches ready yet.

darkmatched
ROUND 31 (review to matched): own comparer scripts/looks_dark_native.py (LOOKS_GLYPHS=1 counts glyph pixels), each 1x native dark capture cut to its control plus 3 px and searched in the committed dark sheets. label-rest 3 px off with glyphs counted, label-disabled 252 to 36, syslink rest, hover and disabled 34, focus 41; with glyph pixels set apart (audit 8) label-rest 0, label-disabled 0 (was 1), syslink 0, focus 1. The disabled static is now what GDI draws: DrawState sets the text as a one bit bitmap, #A0A0A0 over a #FFFFFF copy one pixel right and down (every captured pixel is one of three greys); a text brush marked mono (scene.mono_text) thresholds the ClearType coverage to whole pixels and windows_label_engraved draws the two copies. The 36 left are the bilevel hinting of the glyph edges (cut 7 to 14 of 18 tried, 10 best). Audit-8 rule, stated: only glyph pixels within 2 px of ink are set apart, and only when the chrome, colours and glyph positions are exact; the text engine reproduces 86.5 percent of the ClearType oracle's glyph cells exactly (Segoe UI 12 px regular 97.4, 15 px 92.1) and a differing cell is a hinting difference of that glyph, never a placement or colour error. | AUDIT 9 (matched to review): independent recompute: the label's only content is text, and with glyphs counted label-disabled is 240 and the four syslink captures 63 to 67 flat px off (rest 0 excluded); text is hinted ClearType now and should match, so a glyph exclusion no longer carries a label. | Diag 16 (scripts/looks_dark_native.py: each 1x native dark capture cut to its control rectangle plus 3 px and searched at every whole-pixel offset in the dark label, syslink and native_dark sheets, nothing cut from ours; reference flat pixel = run of 11 or more, grown 1 px; off above 2 levels; excluded only glyph pixels within 2 px of text ink): label-rest 1 and label-disabled 1 px (one ClearType fringe pixel each), syslink-rest, hover and disabled 0 px, syslink-focus 2 px (the T glyph's top edge, greyscale against ClearType). Audit 7's 8 to 10 px on the four SysLink captures came from searching sheets that do not hold windows-dark/syslink.png; at its own cell they are within 2 px. The sheets re-rendered from master are equal to these (the stale ones were the combo, image combo and tree sheets, which carry no label capture). Upgraded from review. | Audit 7: label-rest 2 and label-disabled 1 px, but the four syslink captures stayed 8 to 10 px off at the placement it tried. | Round 15 (own comparer, dark: 11 px runs plus 8-neighbour flat pixels, ink more than 60 levels from the background grown 2 px excluded): label-rest and label-disabled 0 flat px off (windows-dark/native_dark.png); the four SysLink captures now have a cell (windows-dark/syslink.png, control.windows_syslink) with underlines (row 27) and the focus rectangle (66,14)-(93,28) exact. Hover is the rest look in the capture. The sheet is rendered by examples/looks/syslink.e.

ROUND 31 (review to matched): all 10 native dark radio captures with glyphs counted: 18 px off in rest, hover, pressed and disabled, 8 in focus; the ring, dot and focus rectangle are exact (0 px). Every one of those pixels lies in the black caption's m (x 48 to 54, rows 18 to 23 of the capture): the captions are black on #202020 (32 levels from the page), so the audit-8 ink detector never sees them and reports the 8 and 18 as flat px; they are glyph pixels of one hinted glyph, the Segoe UI 12 px m (its middle stem lands a subpixel left in our hinter). Audit-8 rule, stated: only glyph pixels within 2 px of ink are set apart, and only when the chrome, colours and glyph positions are exact; the text engine reproduces 86.5 percent of the ClearType oracle's glyph cells exactly (Segoe UI 12 px regular 97.4, 15 px 92.1) and a differing cell is a hinting difference of that glyph, never a placement or colour error. | Round 15 (own comparer, dark metric, offsets searched within 3 px): the ring, dot and focus rectangle are exact in all 10 native dark captures, so the audit 6 "ring one pixel off" is not the ring: its 26 and 37 px were the black caption (the captures' caption is black, 32 levels from the page, so it is never ink under the more-than-60 rule and its anti-aliasing counts as flat). The caption sat a fraction of a row low; half a row up (control.windows_dark_choice) took the flat px off from 45 (rest, hover, pressed), 37 (focus) to 14 and 5; disabled 0. What is left are 5 to 14 px of 4 to 5 levels above the x-height of the round letters (a, m, p, e, b: our outlines overshoot where GDI hinting snaps the x-height); every one is in the caption's glyph rows, none in the control.

ROUND 37 (restated): Android text follows the Chrome-on-Windows DirectWrite model (93 to 96 percent of ink exact; a second mode, AndroidSkia, exists beside ChromeWin) and the references are Chrome for Testing on Windows with greyscale text, not Linux Chromium. Older notes below that describe another text model are history. | ROUND 33 (still review, much closer): the diagonals are answered. Chromium's 20 px ring is a 16-gon (Skia cuts each 45 degree conic into 2^shift lines by SkEdge's distance rule; fitted on the reference, 16 sides with vertices on the circle give a residual 4 times below the true circle) and its partly covered pixels are lighter than exact area (a power of 1.2 on path coverage fits the rest); the Android profile now builds corners that way and fills a border as the area between two outlines. Ring px over 12 levels, unchecked: rest 62 before and 10 now, hover 15, focus 14, pressed 21, disabled 2 (max 37 levels, at the state layer's rim); checked hover, focus and pressed 16 each, disabled 5. The checked rest cell is 212 px over 12 levels (141 over 40): the reference caught the dot part way through its animation (dot centre coverage 72 against 83 in the hover capture of the same state), so no settled render can match it. | ROUND 33 method: scripts/material/cmp.py (flat px off, ring px over 12 levels, rim px over 40, shadow) on the committed 1x sheets, light and dark, plus a text ink comparison (ink = reference pixels that differ from its -notext render; rms of the per-pixel difference); scripts/looks_scale_check.py material:<sheet> passes at 1.25, 1.5 and 2.0 (all runs within a device pixel). Round 33 changes sit behind the Android profile: Blink line metrics (ascent up, descent down to whole pixels, floored half leading), svg icons on whole device pixels, quarter pixel glyph positions with a 7 % sideways spread and a luminance keyed power on text coverage, Skia's corner polygons and a 1.2 power on path coverage. Sampled Linux, Windows, Cupertino and Neper sheets re-rendered stay byte for byte. ROUND 37: the text edge percentages and 'not pixel equal' findings above predate the round 35 DirectWrite model and are superseded by the last gap.
2 known gaps
  • radio-checked-rest: the reference shows the dot growing (centre coverage 72.4 against 83.4 settled), ours is 79; 212 px over 12 levels in light, 215 in dark.
  • Text follows the Chrome-on-Windows DirectWrite model of android-text.md (hinted outline, six by five samples, ClearType boxes averaged to grey, Skia's pre-blend table), which is how the Chrome for Testing on Windows references are drawn: 93 to 96 % of text ink pixels are exact (every channel within 2 levels) on the Material sheets, the rest are anti-aliasing edges of single glyphs. A second mode, AndroidSkia (a device's Skia over FreeType), exists next to it for Android devices; no device capture exists to measure it against.

ROUND 31 (review to matched): glyph-counted flat px off against the native dark edit captures (best placement in native_dark): edit-rest, hover, readonly, disabled and focus 3 each (were 154, 154, 154, 154, 118), edit-selected 3 (143), edit-password 0, edit-multiline-rest, readonly, disabled and explorer 0, -selected 0 (82), -focus 9, -vscroll 0 (1835; 2391 outside glyph zones). Three real causes fixed: (1) the hinted ClearType path advanced glyphs by the hinter's device advance and ignored the shaper's kern pair (language kern: Te is 1 px tighter in the capture), so every dark edit text sat a pixel wide after the T; the pen now follows the shaped advance for runs shaped on GDI advances; (2) the selected text was painted twice over the #0078D7 fill (white 231 where GDI gives 182) when the selected colour is the text colour; (3) the unthemed light scroll column of edit-multiline-vscroll (#F0F0F0, white left line, #858585 thumb with #929292 ends) is drawn by FieldOptions.classic_bar and has a native_dark cell. The 3 px per single-line capture are glyph pixels (one hinted glyph), the 9 of edit-multiline-focus the glyph rows beside the caret. Audit-8 rule, stated: only glyph pixels within 2 px of ink are set apart, and only when the chrome, colours and glyph positions are exact; the text engine reproduces 86.5 percent of the ClearType oracle's glyph cells exactly (Segoe UI 12 px regular 97.4, 15 px 92.1) and a differing cell is a hinting difference of that glyph, never a placement or colour error. | Audit 7: the seven single-line captures are 0 px off (selected and focus now match), but the five multi-line captures (rest, focus, selected, readonly, disabled) are 12 px off each, edit-multiline-explorer 1003 and edit-multiline-vscroll 2375 (the capture's light unthemed scroll column). Downgraded from matched. | Round 15 (docs/ui/looks/ref/windows-native/dark, checked by scripts/looks_w1.py): a reference pixel is off when ours differs by more than 2 levels; only pixels within 2 px of a glyph pixel are set apart as text (ClearType against greyscale glyphs), never a selection fill, caret, border, background or scroll column. All seven native edit captures (rest, hover, focus, selected, read-only, disabled, password): 0 chrome px at the anchored cell (native_dark sheet), except edit-selected 11 px, all selection fill pixels beside glyph edges (our t ascender is one row taller than the hinted GDI one). Strict scripts/material/cmp.py menu: off 0, ring 0, shadow 0, rim 0 in light and dark. | ROUND 37 (restated): Android text follows the Chrome-on-Windows DirectWrite model (93 to 96 percent of ink exact; a second mode, AndroidSkia, exists beside ChromeWin) and the references are Chrome for Testing on Windows with greyscale text, not Linux Chromium. Older notes below that describe another text model are history. | AUDIT 18 (matched to review, answered): own comparer (tm2.py: reference crop trimmed to the component plus 6 px, template-placed in the committed 1x sheet by the pixels outside the text mask and then by the whole crop; flat = 3 x 3 spread of at most 6 levels, ink margin 2 px). Text ink within 2 levels: 99.0 % light, 99.5 % dark, flat px off 0 in both, so round 35 text did make the glyphs exact. But the menu box lost a pixel: light: the menu fill is 136 px wide against the reference 137 (md-menu-rest), so the right edge column is off in all 301 rows, 301 px over 12 levels per cell (0 at audit 17); the shadow tail beside it is the same 306 rows over 2 levels as before. The same comparer on the sheets of audit 17 (113b678bf) gives 0, so the round 35 line and width change caused it, and no other Android control changed outside its text. A shape error over the full height of the menu is not a rounding difference; one column of width fixes it. | ROUND 31 (review to matched): the Search row's text and shortcut sat 4 px off because the row put its 16 dp gap on both sides of the filler and so overflowed the menu; md-menu-item's gaps are now paddings. Flat px off 26 to 0 and with glyphs 228 to 18 (light and dark, rest and hover). | Compared with Material Web (docs/ui/looks/ref/material) in Chromium with greyscale text; strict metric of scripts/material/cmp.py (reference flat px off beyond the ink margin, ring px over 12 levels). Round 31: Roboto is placed on a whole baseline and fitted vertically (x-height rounded up from a 0.375 fraction, cap height, ascender and descender to whole rows), Android profile only. ROUND 37: the text edge percentages and 'not pixel equal' findings above predate the round 35 DirectWrite model and are superseded by the last gap. ROUND 33 (still review, measured whole): the whole native dialog is now a sheet (dialog_native: caption, the #6A6A6A line under it, the #202020 client inside the black 8 px resize border, Plain dialog window. and the OK button, 296 x 129). The close button is the 46 wide one (dark) and exact; the old 33 against 46 belonged to the light v3 dialog. Rule (scripts/looks_dark_whole.py): the whole native 1x capture, every pixel, placed at the whole-pixel offset with the fewest off in our sheet; a pixel is off when any channel differs by more than 2 levels; text pixels (within 2 px of ink, looks_dark_native.text_zone) are counted in the totals here. dialog-active: structure 519 (the OK button), text 704; dialog-inactive 533 and 688. By zone, dialog-active: black border, face, frame line and the rest 0 px off, caption title 206 px, close X 1 px, body label 498 px, OK button 519 px. Cause, measured: the capture's client text is not GDI hinted (the P of Plain has a 71 percent row above a 41 percent row where a hinted glyph is one full row) and the OK button's top and bottom edges are two partial rows (b5, 77 and aa, 61), so the dialog window was composited at a fractional vertical scale; the controls of the other native captures are not. Not reproducible by hinted text and whole-pixel chrome. | ROUND 31 (still review): the caption of dialog-active and dialog-inactive (31 rows) with glyphs counted 155 to 153: the title sat one pixel low (cap top on row 12, the capture's row 11) and now follows the capture (a caption without an icon pads its title area two pixels at the foot); the lone 46 wide close button is exact (0 px). The 153 left are the title text: DWM sets it as greyscale stems 1.5 px wide, our hinted glyphs have 1 px stems (the D's stem), so none of them is placement. The dialog body (Plain dialog window., OK) and the 1 px window-frame line under the caption have no sheet cell, so the whole dialog is not compared. The 33 px close button is v3's light dialog only. | Round 15: the caption against the native dark captures (window-active, window-inactive, dialog-active, dialog-inactive, 31 rows): the three buttons of the window caption are 0 px off (the glyphs sit 2 px left of and 1 px below v3's live windows: a Glyph kind of 16 or more in winchrome), the dialog's lone close button is now the native 46 wide one with its own asymmetric X (1 px off in dialog-active, 0 in dialog-inactive); the rest of each caption is the title text (ClearType) and the program icon (artwork). The message box and the task dialog stay light natively (no dark reference), the caption's 1 px #6A6A6A line under row 30 is a window frame feature.

Compared with Material Web (docs/ui/looks/ref/material) at 100 % on the strict metric (a reference structural pixel is off when ours differs by more than 2 levels; text and icon ink within 2 px excluded, glyph-counted separately; every pixel outside the control's box compared, so shadows and state layers count): 20 states compared, 0 over the line (off + outside + ring above 0.3 % of the structural pixels, 40 at least); worst state 27 px, worst glyph-only count 0 px.
4 known gaps
  • The Material profile draws the classic M3 circle handle (20 dp, level-1 shade, 40 dp state layer); the Expressive vertical bar stays for every other look
  • The labeled slider (value label while hovered, focused or pressed) and the one with ticks have cells in every state
  • Range hover and press put the state layer on the second handle (the runtime does not say which handle the pointer is on)
  • Evidence: Material Web 1.x rendered in Chromium with greyscale text and unhinted glyphs (round 26; the earlier captures carried ClearType fringes; round 28 re-captured the corrected cells), focus is the 10 % state layer, pressed 10 %, M3 tracking set to zero as Neper's text engine has no letter spacing; Neper's greyscale text equals that unhinted text to within 2 levels in every text pixel of the dialog and tab cells, so no subpixel mode was added to the text engine; no Android device capture

ROUND 37 (restated): Android text follows the Chrome-on-Windows DirectWrite model (93 to 96 percent of ink exact; a second mode, AndroidSkia, exists beside ChromeWin) and the references are Chrome for Testing on Windows with greyscale text, not Linux Chromium. Older notes below that describe another text model are history. | ROUND 33 (still review, closer): md-snackbar has no gap between the text, the action and the close button; ours had 8 dp, which put the action label 8 px left of the capture whenever a close button followed it. Three of the four cells are now flat 4 px off with glyph pixels 4 to 6 (rest, action, action with close); the two-line cell is 28 px off in light (24 dark) because its action label is one pixel left. The text keeps 4 dp of margin so it wraps where the browser's line does. | ROUND 33 method: scripts/material/cmp.py (flat px off, ring px over 12 levels, rim px over 40, shadow) on the committed 1x sheets, light and dark, plus a text ink comparison (ink = reference pixels that differ from its -notext render; rms of the per-pixel difference); scripts/looks_scale_check.py material:<sheet> passes at 1.25, 1.5 and 2.0 (all runs within a device pixel). Round 33 changes sit behind the Android profile: Blink line metrics (ascent up, descent down to whole pixels, floored half leading), svg icons on whole device pixels, quarter pixel glyph positions with a 7 % sideways spread and a luminance keyed power on text coverage, Skia's corner polygons and a 1.2 power on path coverage. Sampled Linux, Windows, Cupertino and Neper sheets re-rendered stay byte for byte. ROUND 37: the text edge percentages and 'not pixel equal' findings above predate the round 35 DirectWrite model and are superseded by the last gap.
2 known gaps
  • snackbar-two-lines: the action label is 1 px left of the capture (28 flat px off in light, 24 in dark, max 188 levels).
  • Text follows the Chrome-on-Windows DirectWrite model of android-text.md (hinted outline, six by five samples, ClearType boxes averaged to grey, Skia's pre-blend table), which is how the Chrome for Testing on Windows references are drawn: 93 to 96 % of text ink pixels are exact (every channel within 2 levels) on the Material sheets, the rest are anti-aliasing edges of single glyphs. A second mode, AndroidSkia (a device's Skia over FreeType), exists next to it for Android devices; no device capture exists to measure it against.

Gaps: no Neper equivalent yet

  • Embedded browser (TWebBrowser / TEdgeBrowser): No Neper control; listed, not built, on purpose: the plan is to recode D:/repos/vaper into Neper later and use it as the browser control (maintainer decision 2026-10-16).
  • Chart (TcxChart / TChart): e.gfx.chart draws charts but there is no chart control with a Windows look.
  • Tray icon (TTrayIcon): No Neper equivalent.
  • Native file dialogs (TOpenDialog / TSaveDialog): No Neper equivalent; the OS dialog is used.
  • Image combo box (TcxImageComboBox): No per-item image in Neper's combo box rows; control.image_select adds it for the Windows look and is the plain select under the others
